Subject: Hosted suitability follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (FinTrend)

Thanks for joining the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right onramp: hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or a Private VPC/on-prem deployment.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: real-time customer support classification + contextual summarization in the product UI.
- Expected growth: pilot month ~100 qps, target production ~300–600 qps over 12 months.
- Latency target: 150–250ms p50 for short responses, occasional longer generation allowed.
- Data requirements: session text only (no file attachments), but must comply with FinTrend's PCI scope — leaning toward isolating sensitive tokens.

Questions to confirm (short answers appreciated)
1) Is data residency or strict VPC/network isolation required for the pilot, or only for scaled production?
2) Peak burst profile: how large are sudden spikes? (e.g., 1k+ concurrent requests for short periods?)
3) Are you able to share a representative payload size (avg tokens in request & response)?

What we recommend next
- Quickstart: we can provision a Hosted sandbox with mapped endpoints and ratecaps so your engineers can exercise the same API and routing logic used in production.
- If you expect sustained >500 rps or strict network isolation for initial launch, Dedicated or Private is the right conversation.

Attachments
- demo-recording.mp4 (screen + narration)
- rate_profile.xlsx (your example traffic & our projection worksheet)

Next steps
- Can you reply with the three short items above?
- If helpful, we'll schedule a 45-minute technical deep dive this week with Ben (runtime/ops) to map endpoints and rate limits.

Thanks — Kim

Thanks Kim — useful recap. Short answers below and a few clarifications so we can move quickly.

Answers
1) For the pilot (first 2 quarters) we prefer Hosted if it keeps traffic & data within a FedRAMP-like region (US). Production will likely require VPC peering or Private VPC for PCI-scoped flows.
2) Peak bursts: we see short spikes up to ~1,200 rps when marketing campaigns hit — typically 2–5 minutes. Average steady-state expected 250–350 rps by launch.
3) Payload sizes: avg request ~1.2k tokens, avg response ~300–500 tokens. Some longer summaries up to 1.5k tokens.

Open questions for Redwood
- What are the hosted sandbox rate limits and how do you recommend mapping endpoints for multiple models (reranker + generator)?
- How quickly can we get a sandbox endpoint with prefix/KV caching enabled for session-based flows?
- If we start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated/Private for production, what does the migration path look like?

We'd like to do the technical dive with Ben on Wed 12/30 at 10:30am PT if that works. If not, any 30–45 min slot this week is fine.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted suitability follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (FinTrend)

Thanks Amit — quick answers and a proposed starter plan.

Short answers
- Hosted sandbox rate limits: by default we provide a sandbox with 150 rps and burst up to 500 rps while we provision trial capacity. We can raise the sandbox ceiling for evaluation with a short capacity request (typical 24–48 hour lead).
- Endpoint mapping: recommended pattern:
  * /v1/generate -> generator model (streaming enabled)
  * /v1/rerank -> small cross-encoder for reranking (lower latency)
  * /v1/emb -> embeddings service (if you use similarity features)
  We expose per-endpoint ratecaps and token-based billing so you can isolate traffic.
- Prefix/KV caching: enabled on Hosted; we can enable session-level KV caching in the sandbox. Caching reduces tokens for repeated context and improves p50 latency.
- Migration path: we support blue/green of model endpoints. Starting on Hosted then committing to Dedicated is straightforward — you pin model versions and routing rules transfer. Private VPC requires a short onboarding (~2–4 weeks) for network/KMS setup.

Starter recommendation (for your pilot numbers)
1) Begin with Hosted sandbox (we'll raise sandbox burst to 800 rps for your evaluation window).
2) Configure endpoint mapping and KV caching; run smoke-test with 1–2 representative payloads.
3) If pilot shows sustained >500 rps and strict network isolation, open the Dedicated evaluation (we'll provide an ROI calc).

I'll attach the Hosted Quickstart Playbook — it includes an endpoint template, recommended ratecaps to start, and a canary routing checklist.

Can confirm Wed 12/30 10:30am PT for the deep dive (Ben, Kim, Amit, Lena). I'll send a calendar invite.
